<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Song of Songs 8:11">Targ. Cant. VIII, 11</cite>.—
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 21b:4">Ab. Zar. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>א׳ אריסותיה קעביד</he> the gentile tenant working during the Jewish festive week, works for his tenancy (not as the Jew’s employee).

<cite ref="Chagigah 25b:16">Ḥag. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>דינא הוא … א׳ וכ׳</he> it is the tenant’s business to procure kegs &c.—*<cite ref="Bava Batra 55a:3">B. Bath. 55ᵃ</cite> <he>דאריסא דפרסאי עד וכ׳</he> Rashb. a. l. (ed. <he>אריסותא</he>, Var. <he>דאֲרִישָׂן</he>, <he>שָׂאִין …</he>, <he>דאֲרִישָׂאָן</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note, Ms. M. <he>דאריש׳</he>) that the tenant of the Persians is such only up to forty years (after which time he is considered a legitimate owner); v. Nim. Jos. to Alf. a. l. [It seems that the Pers. Jews pronounced <cite ref="A03121"><he>אֲרִישָׁא</he></cite> a. <cite ref="A03122"><he>אֲרִישׁוּתָא</he></cite>, cmp. <cite ref="D00746"><he>דִּישְׁתָּנָא</he></cite> a. <cite ref="D00667"><he>דִּיסְתָּנָא</he></cite>.]—Pl. <he>אֲרִיסַיָּא</he>.
